report:
### Conclusion
Your conclusion is correct: **No**, hydroxychloroquine does not reduce the likelihood of dying from COVID-19.

### Key Evidence
Robust evidence from randomized controlled trials and meta-analyses demonstrates that hydroxychloroquine provides no mortality benefit and may increase adverse side effects:

1. **RECOVERY Trial**: This large-scale UK randomized trial evaluated hospitalized COVID-19 patients and found no significant difference in 28-day mortality between the hydroxychloroquine group and standard care, leading researchers to stop the trial arm early (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2022926).
2. **WHO Solidarity Trial**: An international multi-center study led by the World Health Organization concluded that hydroxychloroquine regimens produced little to no effect on 28-day mortality or hospital stay duration (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2023184?query=TOC&page=2).
3. **Cochrane Systematic Review**: A Cochrane review synthesized data across randomized controlled trials and found high-certainty evidence that hydroxychloroquine does not reduce deaths in COVID-19 patients while increasing the risk of adverse events (https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD013587_chloroquine-or-hydroxychloroquine-useful-treating-people-covid-19-or-preventing-infection-people-who).
4. **Meta-Analyses on Mortality**: A comprehensive meta-analysis published in *Nature Communications* analyzing both published and unpublished trial data confirmed that treatment with hydroxychloroquine was not associated with lower mortality (https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-021-22446-z).

Based on these findings, health authorities worldwide recommend against using hydroxychloroquine to prevent or treat COVID-19.
